newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung the most popular top-job candidate - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung the most popular top-job candidate - poll.

text.p: Billionaire shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa is the most popular of the four main candidates for the job of leading Hong Kong after it reverts to China next year, according to the results of poll published on Monday.

Tung was seen by 65.7 percent of those questioned in the poll, conducted by Hong Kong University, as the most suitable of the four candidates for the job, television station TVB said. The maximum rating was 100 per cent.
Former Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang came second in the suitability rating at 61.4 percent. Businessman Peter Woo gained 56.2 percent and former Appeal Court Judge Simon Li 51.1 percent.
However, when asked who they would chose as leader, just 30.2 percent of respondents opted for Tung, 27.5 percent for Yang, 8.7 percent for Woo and 3.3 percent for Li.

TVB did not say whether respondents were asked to choose only from the four candidates, or account for the rest of the respondents in the survey which polled 526 people. It did not say when the poll was conducted.
The British colony of 6.3 million people returns to China at midnight on June 30, 1997 when it becomes a Special Administrative Region of China.
The territory's first post-handover chief executive is expected to be named in December by a 400-strong Beijing supervised group being formed.
Officials from the university were not immediately available for comment.
